I have OCD. Panic attacks and anxiety used to be a daily thing for me. I still have a ton of "triggers" but most days I can rationalize and breathe through them. I started by asking myself if my feelings lined up with reality and if I couldn't say they did, I refused to act on them. I tell myself, "Feelings aren't facts." I have learned to accept that feelings are like road signs notifying me of things I need to pay attention to and I never lie to myself about what I'm feeling.. For me, my anxiety is about control or, more accurately, the possibility of losing control. I have to constantly remind myself that I'm not in control of anyone or anything but me. I play games with myself when I desire control. Every time I think I have figured out a way to grab it, I come up with three plausible but incredibly unlikely things that could happen to prevent me from gaining it. Additionally, I channel my need for routines into productive enterprises. Germ routines are not allowed but showering routines are, etc. This prevents me from turning to a routine in place of dealing with the anxiety. A routine is only allowed if its purpose is to accomplish something which actually needs to be done.

I didn't mean to write a book here. TL:DR I set up conditions for success before anxiety hits and I rarely "give in" to my feelings. I breath through the worst of it and forgive myself for mistakes.

I have anxiety issues 15 years now.

The things that have really helped over that time are:

  • Therapy - Just about to leave talk therapy and moving into CBT. Has really helped exorcise some demons and be comfortable with myself.
  • Being open about it with friends and colleagues so the pressure off about hiding it
  • Diet - The change in mood and just feeling well instead sick after stuffing my face with a Domino's meant for 4 adults
  • Meditation/Mindfulness - The ability to catch my thoughts that would if left to run their course would have me worry myself into an attack is a great thing. Stopping them and bringing my mind back to a rational state
  • Exercise - Yoga, weight lifting, cardio, taking a stroll down the street. Whatever it is, do something. It gets your body into a better state and I have found it allows you to experience sensations like the anxiety triggers (Sweating, heart pumping and breathlessness) but knowing the reason for it and when it comes on in other times it can make it easier to manage.
  • Achievement list - I keep of list all the times I have done something to challenge the anxiety, get my hair cut, driving in heavy traffic etc. It really helps because when I'm anxious it's so hard remember what you really can do.
  • Challenge it when you feel ready - Going into a situation when you already feel unwell is so difficult and leaves you with a bad memory of it. If you can, in a controlled way challenge that situation when you are feeling ready can leave you feeling empowered and with a great memory to reference next time
  • Medication - Take it as long as you feel you need to but also be working on other resources like therapy, exercise and meditation which can lead to you being stronger and may lead to coming of the medication. Use it to get stronger to challenge it. I take some for IBS which acts as an anti depressant as well along with Xanex when things get too much. Take them, don't soldier on.
  • Journal - I have found writing things down not for record keeping but to empty your thoughts from your mind onto a page or computer can help you see things rationally and allow you mind to calm down.
  • Alcohol - Be careful, it can be quiet relaxing and free you from these feeling for a short while. In fact it was the only way for me to feel better for a long time. BUT the after affects and hangover can be devastating. I usually plan the following day to have nothing on so I can relax and not worry but it is something I think you should keep to a bare minimum if you want long term relieve. As /u/1982 said, the list of affects it will have can be brutal
  • Bach Rescue Remedy spray - I use this to get my breath back. 4 sprays into open mouth then inhale usually relaxes my chest and feel I can breathe easier - http://goo.gl/t3l5Z6 also, cold water held in the mouth so that you breathe through nose can be great too.
  • Educate your self - Ok so simply put there will be no magic pill of superhero therapist that is going to make this better. You have to do the work and find out what makes you this way and find the resources to help yourself get better. This haunts you every day then its everyday you have to work on it. When you let your mind slip back to worrying that's when it gains ground.

Really hopes this helps someone even a little.

Keep up the work and you will see results and remember anxiety is part of live, it comes from your view of finances, relationships, work etc. Its up to you to change that view.

So this video is about anxiety related to a video game. But I think it actually says a huge amount about anxiety in general. A researcher is talking about it, and it was so helpful for me.

I avoid anything that seems to exacerbate it, like drinking the day before or lack of sleep. Otherwise I trudge through it, knowing that once the shaking/vibrating stops it'll all seem like it wasn't a big deal afterwards. Also remind myself that a lot of what I'm feeling is merely "The Illusion of Transparency" and that only those especially perceptive or close to me would really notice. It's not perfect, but it's better for me personally than being dependent or reliant on medication (Tried it, screw that).

The biggest help was just not being a pussy. I know that's harsh, but that's the point. Think back to all of those Disney Cartoons and shit... everybody is afraid, but courage is acting in spite of that fear.

So while I can't say the anxiety went away, I just learned to deal with it.

This is by no means easy, but it's not impossible. I spent a good amount of time learning the symptoms. Was I suddenly tapping my foot a bunch or taking quick short breaths? Did the tone of my voice change, etc... Also, what were the causes? Maybe I'm suddenly paranoid that I'm going to die in a car accident is related to the fact that I was watching Fast and Furious earlier.

Then I learned to apply common sense. Am I going to die in a car accident? Maybe, no denying that... but probably not. Billions of people drive every day and don't die. Hell, I myself drive everyday and don't die. Think of all the times where I was positive today was my last, and it wasn't... clearly this anxiety thing is wrong. So although it feels real, realize that it is just a panic attack brought on by a chemical disorder in your brain and everything you're feeling right now is false... an illusion... and worse yet, it's a wrong illusion. If Anxiety was right and reality was wrong, I would have died long before now. So although it might feel like you're about to die... apparently you're not.

I always remember a quote from Buddhism at times like that. "If you have time to worry, you have nothing to worry about".

Which I guess is another thing... I'm a Buddhist and turns out, those teachings help. Fear, anxiety, worry.... they all come from the imagination. You regret things in the past, your afraid of what will happen in the future... but what you need to be focusing on is the present; and right now... everything is fine. You're worried about dying 2 seconds from now... you're focusing on the future, not the present. Currently, you're OK. Focus on that.

Also, it's not necessarily a bad thing. I learned that it's sort of a super power. I mean, anxiety kept me away from a lot of bad things too. I never smoked because I was afraid of cancer. I never did drugs because I was afraid I would get addicted. While Anxiety is a lot of fear in unnecessary places, in places where fear is necessary... I was over prepared. Truth is, I've been waiting for a disaster to happen for so long that in the rare case shit does go to hell, I'm the fucking man on the ball. I'm so use to functioning in complete panic that when everybody else panics I'm King Calm... this state is normal to me... so while everybody is pissing themselves over an earthquake, I'm the one making sure shit is good. Everybody is OK, we're in a safe place, etc...

So I spent some time learning to be calm during a panic attack to be even better at this. Panic Attacks are "Die hard" training. Sure right now you're flipping shit over nothing... but if you can learn to be cool now, when the times comes where you should panic, you'll still be cool... cool like John McClane. In a weird way, this helped a bunch. It was either a fun game, or a training exercise... either way, it was something to focus on instead of just intense panic.

I got chains tattooed on my wrist to help me remember this. I have a broken link at the inside of each wrist... the chains are the anxiety, I have to always wear them... but if I let the anxiety control me then my hands are bound together, the chain link is complete, and I'm a prisoner. Or, I can break the chains and my hands can be free... so, I spent a good amount of time taking deep breaths staring at my own hands trying to remember that this was "sober, normal me thinking" and that "normal me" is correct and I need to trust him in this time of panic.

Over time, it got easier and easier. Sure, I still freak out and panic, but now it's almost like a second thought. Being honest helped too... I just started telling people I'm terrified of everything. Before I was a bit ashamed so I hid it... now days I rock it with pride. "Pretty sure the house is going to fall down and kill us guys... probably a sink hole about to swallow me up any second now. Of course, only after I break all my bones will the brain aneurysm kill me." Now it's almost like an inside joke between me and the people I know.

I'll be driving down the road and I'll just point to a car and be like, "I'm positive that guy is a gang member in training who's going to murder us in a drive by as an initiation into his gang. When he passes us, we're all dead". For some reason, it's just not as terrifying when you say it out loud as it is when you just sit there and think it silently to yourself. Plus, the non-panic from everybody else who now knows what you know, is a big indicator that everything is cool. Then, the guy passes, nobody gets shot, and you remember... again, a billion times people have passed me, and not once have I been shot. Anxiety is an illusion and it's always wrong.

Smoking a little bit of weed helps. Too much and I panic again, but a little bit takes the edge off things. A bong rip and one beer after work is just fantastic. Part of my daily routine includes 15 minutes of just sitting on the couch, being slightly stoned and drinking a beer. It's lazy and I think that's good for me.

Also, I generally spent time trying to improve my life everywhere so I had less to fear. If I thought people were laughing at me behind my back in public I asked myself why I thought that? Sure... Anxiety... but I mean, what did I think they were laughing about? My hair, my clothes? So I tried lots of hair styles until I found one I liked. I went for the "Elija Wood from Wilfred" look. Adult, simple... I bought new clothes, I went to the gym... the gym not only kicks in "feel good brain stuff" but being in better shape was good for my confidence which took away from the, "everybody hates me" anxiety.

So while I still have it, and there is no one thing you can do... you can pick away at it with lots of effort. You just have to face the fear? What are you thinking, why are you thinking that... what can you do to not think that so much... realize that this is all an illusion... act anyway.

How do I get started in D&D?

Well first of all, welcome to DnD! I would expect nothing else to have come from the first session if no one had ever played before, it is a complex game, at least at first.

There is a great YouTube series of some WotC employees playing the starter set for 5e which should help you, as the DM, to understand how things work. Check it out here.

If you have any other specific questions, feel free to continue posting in here and we will answer them for you :)

Regarding spellcasting: every spell will have the information in its description for how it connects with the intended target(s). Typically there are three kinds: "make a ranged spell attack," "the target must make a XXX saving throw," or "the target takes x damage."

To make a ranged spell attack, the player rolls a d20, adds their "spellcasting ability modifier" and compares the result to the targets Armor Class, just like a melee/ranged attack. The spellcasting ability modifier is calculated using the player's spellcasting ability (i.e. Wisdom, Intelligence, Charisma) + proficiency bonus. The cleric for example uses Wisdom as their spellcasting ability as indicated in the player's handbook for that class. So if the cleric has a +3 Wisdom and +2 proficiency then their modifier is +5. Thus, to hit a target they roll 1d20+5 vs enemy AC. Each class uses a different spellcasting ability.

When a targeted creature must make a saving throw then you (the DM) must roll a d20, add (or subtract) the applicable ability score modifier for that particular creature and compare the result to the casting player's "spell save DC." The spell save DC is calculated similarly to the spellcasting ability modifier: 8 + spellcasting ability + proficiency. Going with the same stats for the cleric again, it would be 8 + 3 + 2 = 13. Any spells the players cast use this same formula if a target ever has to make a saving throw.

And finally there are spells that just do x damage. If there is nothing else in the description text and it just does damage then the player rolls for damage and it is applied accordingly.

Edit: Sacred Flame is the second of these two types. The text states that the creature must succeed on a Dexterity Saving Throw or take 1d8 radiant damage.

I'm definitely an uber noob at D&D but I'm diving in headfirst, throwing caution to the wind. I've spent the last day and a half writing the core of a campaign. I don't know anything about how to make one, so it will probably be pretty terrible at first, but here's a screenshot of the Google Doc I'm building it in (I jacked the image from Google): http://i.imgur.com/WjkheHx.png

I used the 5x5 method of story writing which was insanely helpful in developing my story from start to finish. I have 5 acts, and each act has 5 chapters. Each chapter is about 30 minutes to 2 hours of gameplay, depending of course on countless factors. I tried to avoid "railroading" players onto a linear path but there is a main story that is only progressed by certain actions.

I'm really excited to play this new campaign as soon as I finish it up. If it's successful I might share the Google doc on here so others can play it and/or improve it.

The story is likely non-canon for D&D stuff but for the most part it should be pretty accurate to the creatures, spells, etc.

Anyway I am just really happy to be part of this community and game. I have wanted to play it for so long and timing was finally right. I have a large enough group of beginners to the game who all really want to play it.

I'm really geeking out on my story. Spoiler: toward the end of the game, Krull (pronounced like "hole") is so empowered with dark magic that he uses a nearby volcano as a weapon.

This is what DnD is all about, play and learn and you will see what works and what doesn't. The biggest warning every new DM should keep in mind is that players think differently than you: don't plan on them doing what you would do because it is 100% guaranteed that they will do the opposite :).

Good luck and have fun!
